solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lifeless hair? There's no spring in it

parts.note: lifeless means dead
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: A limp hairstyle is mocked as having no bounce at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's no spring in it' sounds like a jibe about the hair, but it defines the answer: a deadlock is a lock worked only by a key, with no spring latch.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock bolt is moved by the key alone, unlike a spring latch that snaps shut by itself.

clue.text: Assistant forgoing record tax

indicators.note: forgoing means going without, so the record's letters are dropped from the assistant

parts.note: a deputy is an assistant or second-in-command
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An assistant skipping the payment of tax on a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is a levy charged by government, especially on imported goods, so it is a kind of tax.

clue.text: Place to gamble with mature, Damascene conversion

indicators.note: a conversion changes one thing into another, so these letters are turned into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grown-up gambler has a sudden road-to-Damascus change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damascene conversion' is a stock phrase for a sudden change of belief, which hides that 'conversion' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a hall of slot machines and coin-operated games where people bet small sums.

clue.text: Catalogue containing old book by political operator

indicators.note: containing means holding something inside, so the list wraps the other pieces

parts.note: a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A political fixer holds a catalogue that includes an old book.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobbyist works to influence legislators on behalf of an interest group, an operator in politics.

clue.text: Vegetable, cold and difficult to chew

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
hard food is difficult to chew

explanation.surface: A cold vegetable that is tough to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green, the beet relative also called Swiss chard, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Clubs depressed bridge team, not the brightest people?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
depressed means low in spirits
North and South form one partnership at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A gloomy bridge team at a club is judged a bit dim.
explanation.definitionFit: Clowns are fools or buffoons, so they are playfully cast as people lacking intelligence.

clue.text: Poet, fat and benevolent, neglecting daughters

indicators.note: neglecting means leaving out, so the daughters' letters are dropped

parts.note: lard is pig fat
benevolent means kind
D is the abbreviation for daughter; two daughters give two Ds

explanation.surface: A poet described as plump and generous, but not to his daughters.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking a D from both LARD and KIND leaves LAR and KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was an English poet, author of The Whitsun Weddings and High Windows.

clue.text: Unexpected gains in turn decline for spells

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as with a handle
a fall is a decline
pro means for, in favour of
fits are spells or bouts of something

explanation.surface: Gains that come and go in fits and starts, now up, now down.
explanation.definitionFit: Windfall profits are sudden large earnings not planned for, often from a jump in market prices.

clue.text: Gloomy corner church artist has come in to draw

parts.note: SE, south-east, names a corner of a map or room

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the church and artist sit inside the pull

parts.note: to draw is to pull
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist sits in a church corner, dismally sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepulchral means tomb-like, hence dismal and funereal in mood or tone.

clue.text: Pick source of radioactivity on particle

parts.note: to elect is to pick or choose

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Choosing where radioactivity comes from, on the particle level.
explanation.definitionFit: An electron is the negatively charged subatomic particle that orbits an atom's nucleus.

clue.text: Small picture that's reduced by 50 per cent in album unfortunately

indicators.note: cutting by half keeps only the first two of its four letters

parts.note: that's is that is, read here as the word that

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A photo shrunk to half size in an album, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Halving THAT keeps TH; 'unfortunately' then jumbles IN and ALBUM to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail is a tiny preview image, named for being roughly the size of a fingernail.

clue.text: Called, cancelling start of general preparatory period

indicators.note: cancelling means wiping out, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: rung up means telephoned, called

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone phoned to call off the beginning of a general's preparations.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up is the lead-in time before an event, such as the run-up to an election.

clue.text: Attractive forests are finally encountering axes

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: x and y are the axes of a graph

explanation.surface: Forests looking appealing as the axes come.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexy means sexually appealing, and loosely exciting or attractive in general.

clue.text: Deft clue I recast is misleading

indicators.note: recasting something gives it a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smart clue that has been rewritten turns out to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceitful means given to deceiving, so it describes someone or something that misleads.

clue.text: Runs off after snatching coat, to be precise

indicators.note: snatching means grabbing hold of, so the runner takes in the coat

parts.note: splits is slang for leaves or runs off
an animal's coat is its hair

explanation.surface: A thief flees after grabbing a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To split hairs is to make overly fine distinctions, being fussily exact about small points.

clue.text: Green spots in food store leading to no serious comment

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the meadows go within the food store

parts.note: a pantry is a room where food is kept
leas are meadows, green pieces of land

explanation.surface: Mouldy green patches in the larder lead to a quip.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a polite joke or light remark, not meant to be taken seriously.

clue.text: Note rise of US writer they condemned as a mere beginner

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads upward, so the writer's name runs backwards

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

indicators.note: condemned suggests something ruined, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A note on the rise of an American writer whom critics dismissed as a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a newcomer or novice, originally a new convert to a religion.

clue.text: Pencil marking circling a line rejected as nonsense

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the result is read backwards
circling means going round, so the pencil grade surrounds the other letters

parts.note: HB is the grading stamped on a standard pencil

explanation.surface: A pencil grade drawn round a line is dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah is informal for empty talk or drivel, as in blah blah blah.

clue.text: Excellent sewer sequestering carbon in damaging fluid

indicators.note: sequestering means shutting away, so carbon is enclosed

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as AI
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
a drain is a sewer

explanation.surface: A fine sewer that traps carbon in a harmful liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) is treated as the letters AI, and C goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is precipitation polluted by sulphur and nitrogen oxides that harms forests and buildings.

clue.text: Letter from nine written in reverse

indicators.note: written in reverse means set down backwards

parts.note: nine letters run from A to I, written A TO I

explanation.surface: A letter is the ninth, counted backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From nine' seems to point at the ninth letter of something; instead it describes the run A to I, the first nine letters, which read backwards spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, a nice touch given the nine in the clue.

clue.text: Abundance of banality? More work required, with one change

parts.note: corn is trite, sentimental material

indicators.note: one change means a single letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Utopia is the book by Sir Thomas More

explanation.surface: A critic finds the piece banal and says it needs more work, with one change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' looks like 'extra', but it is Thomas More; changing UTOPIA's T to C gives UCOPIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornucopia is the horn of plenty, so by extension an overflowing supply.

clue.text: Something burning up oxygen in measuring device

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so oxygen goes within the device

parts.note: a meter is an instrument that measures
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Something uses up oxygen inside a gauge.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a space rock that burns up as it streaks through the atmosphere, a shooting star.

clue.text: Waters garden bordering river in curved shape

indicators.note: bordering means lying on either side, so the hoses go round the river

parts.note: to hose is to water, as a garden
to hoe is to work a garden

explanation.surface: Watering a garden next to a river that bends round.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe is a U-shaped iron, so the name stands for any shape bent like one.

clue.text: Very much forgetting day in the remote past

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving out, so the day is dropped

parts.note: dearly means very much, as in love dearly

explanation.surface: Someone who loved the old days very much but has forgotten them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition fits the answer as in early times, long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Early refers to an ancient period, as in early man or the early Church.

clue.text: Party goer regularly finding the way out?

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A partygoer keeps finding the exit.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is how one leaves a room, though equally the way in, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Way of working will fill a second book

indicators.note: filling means going into, so MO sits inside the others

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A method that will fill out a sequel.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: Picture I get by removing a name

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: to manage is to get by, cope

explanation.surface: Someone imagines coping after dropping a name.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a representation of something, a picture or likeness.

clue.text: Circulating damp polluted air in strange plant-holder

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the word is turned back

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax in water, to dampen it

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the jumbled air goes within the strange

parts.note: rum means odd or strange

indicators.note: polluted means fouled, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Damp, dirty air circulates in an odd container for plants.
explanation.walkthrough: RET reversed gives TER; AIR jumbled is ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrarium is a glass enclosure where small plants are grown, like an indoor mini-garden.

clue.text: Queen and King tucking into quiet drink

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the royals sit within the quiet

parts.note: shy means quiet and reserved
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
R, Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: The royals tuck into a quiet drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from Spain, typically served as an aperitif.

clue.text: Henry is working to block agent, backing mind-control

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the result is read backwards
blocking means sitting in the way, so these words go inside the spy

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: A man is busy obstructing an agent, while supporting brainwashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is working' reads as a phrase, IS ON, and 'backing' applies to the whole insertion, not just the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnosis induces a trance in which a subject responds to suggestion, a form of controlling the mind.
